title: Korea Post says hackers looked up recipient details of registered mail via mobile service
date_note: Edaily's page, published 27 November, says the ministry and Postal Services Headquarters confirmed the leak that day; the access itself ran 17 to 24 November.
geo_basis: country: the article names the Postal Services Headquarters, no city
summary: Edaily reports the Ministry of Science and ICT and the Postal Services Headquarters confirmed that hackers used the delivery-location change feature of the mobile Internet Post Office to look up names, addresses and phone numbers of recipients of registered mail from the 17th to the 24th. Analysis of one day's data confirmed 113,855 customers, including corporate entities, and the full scope is still being investigated.
plain: Hackers looked up names, addresses and phone numbers of people receiving registered mail through a Korea Post mobile feature. Officials confirmed 113,855 people so far; the total is still being checked.
exec: Korea Post's recipient data was looked up through a mobile feature; officials confirmed 113,855 customers so far and the full scope is under investigation.
action: The Postal Services Headquarters head warns customers to be wary of messages demanding additional shipping fees and to check with the Postal Customer Center (1588-1300).

evidence.quote: 현재까지 분석이 완료된 하루 분량의 정보에서 개인정보가 유출된 고객은 법인을 포함해 11만3855명으로 확인됐다.

validation.note: Only Edaily was read; it relays the ministry's and Postal Services Headquarters' statement.
